usCourseworkText: Supplemental courses and content strongly recommended include: Microbiology, Genetics, Calculus, Statistics, Immunology, Humanities and Social Sciences
additionalCoursework:
Suggested: 
Readiness for success as a medical student requires above-average reading comprehension and critical thinking skills; quantitative and analytical reasoning; familiarity with scientific inquiry; and a solid foundational understanding of the systems of the human body. Therefore, while not required to apply to UNR Med, the following courses are strongly recommended and will provide you with the readiness for professional, graduate-level studies. 

-Anatomy & Physiology
-Upper-division courses in cell biology, genetics, immunology, molecular biology, metabolic regulation, statistics/bio-stats, neurobiology, microbiology, and calculus
-Courses that examine the psychological, economic, systemic, and socio-cultural factors that influence the health and well-being of individuals and populations;
-Courses in medical history, literature, and ethics.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine is an inclusive and engaged community and recognizes the value that students, faculty and staff from different backgrounds promotes excellence in education, research and health care. Our school  create space for inclusive conversation and education by hosting monthly Diversity Dialogues, a quarterly Diversity Health Series, and an annual Inclusive Medicine Lecture Series. 

The Office of Admissions is engaged in a variety of initiatives and programs to inspire, educate and support prospective students from groups underrepresented in medicine and from medically underserved rural and low-income communities.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Student-requested leaves of absence due to illness or any other emergency are to be made to the Associate Dean for Admissions and Student Affairs.  After counsel with the Student Promotions and Conduct Committee (SPCC), the Associate Dean will make a recommendation to the UNSOM Dean.  Approval is either granted or denied by the Dean.  Students who request a leave of absence are expected to attend classes and continue to be students in good standing until such leave is granted.  Leaves of absence are not granted for students experiencing academic difficulty.  Students who are on a leave of absence are not eligible to receive financial aid and may be required to start paying off existing student loans.  A leave of absence may create a gap in a student's professional timeline that will be of concern to residency program directors, state medical boards, credentialing and various other entities. medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Medical students at the University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine are active in all parts of the school, from participating as voting members on all school committees;  engaging in  educational outreach and mentoring programs for pre-med students; and serving as student leaders in clubs and organizations. Students are supported in starting new activities or programs, and can apply to complete longitudinal scholarly concentrations.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine, a research-intensive, community-based medical school, is located at the base of the beautiful Sierra Nevada Mountains. With Lake Tahoe 30 minutes to the west, the Black Rock Desert to the northeast, and Yosemite a short road trip to the southwest, Reno is a great destination for nature lovers and outdoor recreation enthusiasts. The mid-sized city of Reno offers an abundance of cultural events, highly-rated restaurants, and top-tier entertainment. The medical school campus is located on a beautiful 290-acre campus just north of downtown and includes the Center for Molecular Medicine, the Center for Bioinformatics, the Family Medicine Center, and Health Sciences and Medical Education buildings.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus graduate and professional housing is available as well as off-campus housing within short distances from campus.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
UNR Med's student interest group, MedPride, is dedicated to supporting future doctors who are committed to improving healthcare and access to care for the LGBTQIA+ community. Students collaborate with faculty and staff to increase the conversation and visibility of LGBTQIA+ within and across the curriculum at UNR Med.

To both create an inclusive community and to introduce all first-year medical students to providing care to LGBTQIA+ patients, UNM Med provides a program comprised  lecture on sexual orientation in medicine and transgender health — along with peer-led training in sexual history-taking of transgender patients, peer-led transgender case studies involving LGBTQIA+ issues, Safe Zone training and a panel discussion with LGBTQIA+ patients and providers.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The School of Medicine's Learning and Wellness Resource Center (LWRC) addresses several different areas of wellness including mental, emotional, physical activity, nutrition and social.  See our website for information on our wellness programs and events. https://med.unr.edu/community/student-outreach-clinic
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: One of the four pillars of UNR Med’s mission statement is a commitment to maintaining a culture of diversity and inclusion, as this will enhance excellence in teaching, research, and patient care. In alignment with our core values to improve and innovate, to serve with integrity, and to acheive success through trust and respect, UNR Med hosts many affinity groups, such as the Latino Medical Student Association, Student National Medical Association, Asian Pacific Islander American Medical Student Association, South Asian Medical Student Association, Medical Student Pride Alliance, as well as student interest groups related to disability and chronic illness, and that support students from first generation, low income, and rural backgrounds. The larger Reno and university community is highly diverse and has rich cultural offerings through organizations such as the Northern Nevada Black Cultural Awareness Society, the Latino Research Center, and the Hispanic Chamber of Commerce.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Learning and Wellness Resource Center provides comprehensive academic support and  services to support the physical, mental, and emotional well-being of our students.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Early clinical training and preceptorships provide students with training in health assessments, doctor/patient relationship skills, physical examination and diagnosis.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: We employ collaborative and cooperative instructional methods that include traditional and Socratic lectures; simulation/standardized patients; case studies; and team based learning activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clerkships include Family Medicine, Psychiatry, Internal Medicine, Neurology, Surgery, Pediatrics, OB/GYN, an advanced clinical rotation in Rural Health and four weeks of Selectives.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: MedFIT is a required one-week course that combines a traditional orientation with an introduction to the academic curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Unless otherwise stated by the course or block director, attendance at lectures is highly encouraged.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The primary goal of UNR Med is to develop caring, responsible, skillful, and knowledgeable physicians capable of delivering high quality health care. Students are taught to be sensitive to the needs of their patients, their patients' families, and to their own needs as individuals and as physicians. The curriculum emphasizes interpersonal and professional skills development . We encourage students to develop self-directed learning skills of critical thinking, problem solving, self-assessment, information appraisal, and to prepare for lifelong learning as a physician. It is expected that UNR Med graduates will feel a responsibility not only to treat the ill but also to become leaders in the effort to promote and maintain health in the community in which they practice.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Programs include: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics and Advanced Clinical Experience in Rural Health Care.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
The University of Nevada, Reno is a Carnegie® R1 research university committed to the pursuit of knowledge that addresses the important issues of our time, promotes innovation and drives Nevada's economic prosperity.

Research is an integral part of our medical students' educational experience. The School of Medicine holds nearly $60 million in multi-year, National Institutes of Health (NIH) research grants for studies into the causes and treatments for diseases including muscular dystrophy, gastrointestinal disorders, HIV, fertility, cancer, infectious diseases, and battlefield injuries. The basic science departments boast two of three (and collaborate in the third) Center of Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE) grants, the only IDeA Network of Biomedical Research Excellence grant.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: The School of Medicine offers opportunities for added distinction through Scholarly Concentrations, research, and dual degrees programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: UNR Med houses the Student Outreach and Rural Outreach Clinics, a student managed center that delivers care to the underserved in Reno and our regional rural communities.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students have access and are encouraged to participate in research and have the option to pursue a scholarly concentration in various areas of focus.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: UNR Med is affiliated with Renown Health and actively collaborates with the Veteran's Administration Sierra Nevada Healthcare System; Northern Nevada Medical Center; and St. Mary's Medical Center,
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: First and second year courses are graded as Pass/Fail. Third and fourth year courses are graded as Honors, High Pass, Pass, Fail.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Since 1969, the University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine has prepared students, residents and fellows to lead the way to better health. With support from local physicians and clinical partners, and in affiliation with Renown Health, we educate and prepare our learners to deliver compassionate care to patients in our local community and throughout rural Nevada. 

With an incoming cohort of just 70 students each year, UNR Med offers a small community feel where everyone is connected and engaged. Our on-site Learning and Wellness Resource Center offers academic support, counseling resources, and a focus on health and wellness. Students receive exposure to clinical environments almost immediately upon enrollment, active inter-professional training, access to medical simulation technology, opportunities to engage in research, and scholarly concentrations are available in a variety of specialties with a longitudinal research component.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The mission of the University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine is to improve the health and well-being of all Nevadans and their communities. We achieve our mission through an institutional commitment to diversity and inclusion and a commitment to excellence in education, research, and clinical care.  

At UNR Med, we recognize that people are our strength; and our core values include a commitment to improve and innovate; to serve with integrity, and to succeed with trust and respect.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The Post-Baccalaureate (Post-Bac) Pathway Program is a supportive, one-year academic program for students seeking admission to the University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine (UNR Med). Our program provides a structured, on campus curriculum for individuals who have encountered prior academic challenges to further develop and demonstrate academic readiness for medical school. Post-Bac students complete 30-34 credits of upper-division coursework at the University of Nevada, Reno to fill in any gaps in their science education, and to support their preparation for medical school and success on standardized exams, including an intensive MCAT preparatory course. The program also includes regular check-ins with a learning specialist to help set and achieve professional development goals that support success as future UNR medical students.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Letters from family, friends, parents' colleagues, or others with a personal relationship to the applicant will not be accepted.

REAPPLICANTS: If you are reapplying to UNR Med, the admissions committee will accept two (2) letters of evaluation from the immediate past application cycle as long as they were written no more than two (2) years prior to the date you apply and meet all current requirements. The third letter must be new and dated for the current admission cycle year.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: UNR Med requires three letters of evaluation. Letters must include (1) an academic evaluation written by an instructor or faculty member with direct knowledge of your commitment to academic excellence and who can provide information about your thinking and reasoning skills as well as professional competencies that directly impact academic performance; (2) a clinical evaluation written by a physician (MD or DO), a Nurse Practitioner, or a Physician Assistant who can evaluate, based upon direct observation, your performance within a clinical environment, including engagement or care to patients, your passion for medicine, and your professional competencies. The third letter of evaluation (3) may be written from any reference who can assess your competencies, attributes, and experiences for medical school and a career as a physician.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
RESIDENCY, GPA AND MCAT APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS

As a Nevada state institution of higher education, the admissions committee gives interview and admission preference to applicants who currently reside in Nevada as DACA or legal residents; who graduated from a Nevada high school or college/university; whose parents reside in Nevada, or; who are stationed in Nevada with the armed forces. 

INSTATE APPLICANTS
***Please note changes to the GPA and MCAT requirements starting in 2026
To be reviewed as an Instate applicant requires meeting all Category A criteria outlined at https://med.unr.edu/education/medical-education/md-admissions-process . This includes having a cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.3 or above from an accredited U.S. university; a 3.5 cumulative GPA in 30 credits or more of post-baccalaureate or graduate courses; or a 3.5 GPA in a completed graduate degree; AND an MCAT of 500 or above. 

OUT-OF-STATE APPLICANTS
***Please note the addition of Washington state to our list of accepted residence states starting in 2026
Approximately 100 out-of-state applicants are invited to interview to fill approximately 10% of the incoming class of 70 students. 

Applications are accepted from Non-Nevada residents with legal or DACA residence in Alaska, Arizona,  California, Idaho, Montana, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming. Applications are also accepted from individuals who previously lived in Nevada or if their spouse, partner, or a member of their immediate or extended family is verified to be a current legal Nevada resident. 

Non-Nevada applicants, who meet the criteria above, must have an MCAT of 500 or above and one of the following; cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.30 or above from an accredited U.S. university; a 3.5 cumulative GPA in 30 credits or more of post-baccalaureate or graduate courses; or a 3.5 GPA in a completed graduate degree.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: UNR Med Interviews begin in August and conclude in January.
Deadline to submit regular pool MD application.

Notification of decisions for general pool of MD applications begins.  Decision notifications are delivered via email on the 20th of each month until March 20, unless the 20th falls on a holiday or weekend. In that case, decisions will be sent the next working day.

Accepted applicants must "commit to enroll" at UNR Med by using the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School tool by April 30 or by the date on their acceptance letter. Accepted applicants who are alternates on another school's waitlist may continue to "plan to enroll" at UNR Med after April 30, but must make a final commitment by June 15. Extension requests are considered on a case-by-case basis.
The final day to commit to matriculate at UNR Med and withdraw from waitlists at other medical schools is June 17.  Requests for extensions are considered on a case-by-case basis.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Candidates are notified by March 20 if they have been selected as an alternate. Candidates may request information about position on waitlist after April 30.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
UNR Med is engaged in a comprehensive review of prerequisite requirements.  

Updates to the following requirements will be posted at: https://med.unr.edu/education/medical-education/md-admissions-process

Biology: 15 credits including 6 credits of upper division and 2 credits of lab
Chemistry: 8 credits, including 2 credits of lab)
Organic Chemistry: 8 credits including 2 credits of lab 
Physics: 8 credits, including 2 credits of lab
Psychology or Sociology: 3 credits
Biochemistry: 3 credits 
 
Virtual coursework is accepted
medSchoolSelection.premedCourseworkNote: Note: Additional 3 hours each for Upper Division Biological Science; cell/molecular biology, genetics, calculus, statistics, and immunology strongly recommended.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
UNR Med is committed to a comprehensive, individual, and balanced  review of each candidate's application. We seek students who share our core values, who will add to our culture of diversity and inclusion, and who share our vision of a healthy Nevada. 

We seek students who demonstrate an informed and mature passion for medicine; whose experiences have resulted in the development of social and communication skills, sensitivity to others, cultural awareness, integrity, and a collaborative approach, and; who exhibit a commitment to learning, improving and innovating, and to applying knowledge in the service of others.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText:
In preparation for the application process, candidates should acquire significant exposure to physicians, healthcare, and medicine in order to demonstrate and develop a mature understanding of the responsibilities of being a physician, of the challenges of practicing medicine, and awareness of how being a physician differs from other healthcare roles. 

Candidates are encouraged to seek exposure in various clinical environment and to shadow an array of specializations while acquiring experiences interacting with and caring for patients. In addition, candidates are encouraged to engage in service opportunities that develop compassion, cultural sensitivity and that demonstrate a commitment to their local community.
